translation.text:
The vision that I saw[a], brothers, came twenty days after the former vision; it was as a pattern of the tribulation that is coming.

I was going into the countryside by the Campanian road. It is about ten stadia from the public road, and the place is easy to travel.

So, walking alone, I was beseeching the Lord to bring to completion the revelations and the visions that he had shown me through his holy Church, so that he would strengthen me and give repentance[m] to his servants who have stumbled, in order that his great and glorious name might be glorified, because he counted me worthy to show me his wonders.

And while I was glorifying and giving thanks to him, something like the sound of a voice answered me: “Do not be double-minded, Hermas.” I began to reason within myself and say, “What do I have to be double-minded about, being so firmly established by the Lord and having seen glorious things?”

I went on a little, brothers, and behold, I see dust rising as if to the sky, and I began to say within myself, “Perhaps cattle are coming and stirring up dust?” For it was about a stadion away from me[b].

As the dust grew greater and greater, I supposed it was something divine. The sun shone out a little, and behold, I see a very great beast, like some sea monster, and from its mouth fiery locusts were coming out. The beast was about a hundred feet in length, and its head was like a jar.

I began to weep and to ask the Lord that he would deliver me from it. And I remembered the word that I had heard: “Do not be double-minded, Hermas.”

So then, brothers, having put on the faith of the Lord and having remembered the mighty deeds that he had taught me, I took courage and gave myself over to the beast. Now the beast was coming with such a rushing roar that it could ravage a city.

I came near it, and that huge sea monster stretched itself out on the ground and did nothing except thrust out its tongue; it did not move at all until I had passed by it.

Now the beast had four colors on its head: black, then fiery and blood-red, then golden[l][k][j][i][h][g][f][e][d][c], then white.

footnotes.text: “As a pattern” translates εἰς τύπον—literally, “as a type.” Early Christians used τύπος for prefigurative images.
The Campanian road likely refers to a Roman route leading toward Campania from Rome.
“Through his holy Church”: In earlier visions Hermas receives revelations mediated by a woman who personifies the Church.
“Do not be double‑minded” echoes the ethical vice of divided loyalty; compare James 1:6–8.
“Herds”: κτήνη can mean domestic animals in general; alternatives include “beasts” or “cattle.”
κῆτος denotes a large sea creature or sea‑monster; “whale” is another possible rendering.
Fiery locusts evoke apocalyptic imagery; compare Joel 2 and Revelation 9.
“Its head was like earthenware”: κεραμος can mean tile, pottery, or clay vessel—the simile is obscure.
“Deliver” renders a verb from the ransom/deliverance word‑group (λυτρ‑); alternatives include “rescue” or “ransom.”
“Putting on faith” uses clothing imagery for virtue; compare 1 Thessalonians 5:8.
Or 'Now the beast was approaching with a rushing roar, so that it could ravage a city.'.

Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Use repentance for moral change while preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness, conduct and the angel of repentance; do not impose a different tradition on it.

lexical_decisions.rationale: τύπος in early Christian usage often denotes a foreshadowing or exemplar; “pattern” keeps the typological sense while remaining readable. Footnote preserves the technical term 'type'.
θλῖψις commonly denotes eschatological or communal pressure; 'tribulation' retains that weight and apocalyptic register.
While ἀγρός can be a specific field, the Roman-road setting suggests the rural outskirts; 'countryside' fits the scene.
A Roman context likely referring to a road toward Campania; 'road' is plain and accurate; capitalization signals a proper route name.

alternatives: about a mile and a quarter
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retaining the ancient unit preserves texture; a footnote supplies the modern estimate.
δημόσιος modifies ὁδός as the main, public thoroughfare; 'highway' conveys that nuance.
Idiomatic English equivalent of 'easy to travel' with walking imagery retained.
In prayerful context, 'beseech' captures earnest petition better than neutral 'ask'.
Established pair; 'revelations' and 'visions' are distinct yet complementary; avoid flattening.
Conveys the idea of completing what has been begun without the misleading connotations of 'perfect' in modern English.

alternatives: by means of his holy assembly
lexical_decisions.rationale: Hermas personifies the Church as a visionary mediator; 'Church' with capitalization preserves that identity.
'Strengthen' is the conventional and clear rendering in prayer contexts.

review_passes.summary: The draft is highly accurate and captures the apocalyptic register well. A few minor adjustments were made for consistency (translating ἰδοὺ βλέπω identically in adjacent verses) and to correct awkward English phrasing ('gave myself toward' and 'from me about a stadion away').
issues_found: Inconsistent translation of 'ἰδοὺ βλέπω' in v. 5 ('see! I notice') compared to v. 6 ('look! I see').
Awkward English word order in v. 5: 'For it was from me about a stadion away.'
Unnatural English phrasing in v. 8: 'I gave myself toward the beast' for 'εἰς τὸ θηρίον ἐμαυτὸν ἔδωκα'. 'I gave myself over to the beast' is more idiomatic while retaining the reflexive force.

I was going into the countryside by the Campanian road. It is about ten stadia from the public road, and the place is easy to travel.

So, walking alone, I was beseeching the Lord to bring to completion the revelations and the visions that he had shown me through his holy Church, so that he would strengthen me and give reorientation[m] to his servants who have stumbled, in order that his great and glorious name might be glorified, because he counted me worthy to show me his wonders.

And while I was glorifying and giving thanks to him, something like the sound of a voice answered me: “Do not be double-minded, Hermas.” I began to reason within myself and say, “What do I have to be double-minded about, being so firmly established by the Lord and having seen glorious things?”

I went on a little, brothers, and behold, I see dust rising as if to the sky, and I began to say within myself, “Perhaps cattle are coming and stirring up dust?” For it was about a stadion away from me[b].

translation.text: So, walking alone, I was beseeching the Lord to bring to completion the revelations and the visions that he had shown me through his holy Church, so that he would strengthen me and give repentance[a] to his servants who have stumbled, in order that his great and glorious name might be glorified, because he counted me worthy to show me his wonders.

translation.text: And while I was glorifying and giving thanks to him, something like the sound of a voice answered me: “Do not be double-minded, Hermas.” I began to reason within myself and say, “What do I have to be double-minded about, being so firmly established by the Lord and having seen glorious things?”

simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB base text and source image
simplification_decisions.rationale: The clear past-tense wording retains the vivid skyward image without adding suddenness.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: For it was about a stadion away from me
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: The dust was about 200 yards away from me
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The observed disturbance, not the conjectured cattle, was roughly one stadion distant.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB base text, discourse referent, and historical measure
simplification_decisions.rationale: Naming the dust avoids confirming the cattle and converts the ancient measure approximately.

risk_flags.risk: A stadion did not have one universally fixed length.
risk_flags.mitigation: “About 200 yards” gives a familiar rounded equivalent while retaining approximation.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: I went a little farther, brothers, and suddenly I saw dust rising toward the sky. I thought, “Perhaps cattle are coming and stirring up the dust.” They were about 200 yards away from me.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The ordinary-language movement phrase and the approximate conversion of a stadion to 200 yards are clear and warranted. Revision is needed because the final plural pronoun confirms cattle that the narrator only supposes are coming. The replacement keeps the observed dust, rather than the conjectured cattle, as the thing at a distance. It also removes “suddenly,” which is not required by the base wording, while retaining the vivid skyward image in accessible language.

simplification_decisions.rationale: Adding “shaped” clearly expresses the physical comparison.

risk_flags.mitigation: The wording preserves both this ambiguity and the tentative nature of his thought.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: As the dust grew thicker and thicker, I thought it must be something divine. The sun shone through faintly, and there before me I saw an enormous beast resembling a sea monster. Fiery locusts came from its mouth. The beast was about a hundred feet long, and its head was shaped like a jar.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The revision is substantially clearer and its visual clarifications are warranted by the immediate scene: dust makes faint sunlight intelligible, and “shaped like a jar” naturally states the physical comparison. It also properly retains the ambiguity of “something divine.” Revise only the added “must,” which overstates the tentative supposition in the POB.

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: begged the Lord to rescue me from it

simplification_decisions.rationale: The direct wording expresses the plea in natural modern English.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: I began to cry and begged the Lord to rescue me from it. Then I remembered the words I had heard: “Do not be divided in your mind, Hermas.”

Retain the remembered saying as singular, however; “message” preserves the POB’s singular while reading naturally in modern English. The unresolved referent of “it” is appropriately retained rather than guessed.

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: remembered the mighty deeds he had taught me about

simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB controlling meaning and immediate syntax
simplification_decisions.rationale: Adding “about” makes the relationship between the teaching and the deeds natural in English.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: I took courage and gave myself over to the beast
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: This gave me courage, and I gave myself up to the beast
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Remembering gave him courage to surrender himself to the beast.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB controlling meaning and independent grounding review
simplification_decisions.rationale: The revision keeps the active self-surrender that the earlier draft weakened.

risk_flags.risk: “Gave myself up” may suggest defeat or capture to some readers.
risk_flags.mitigation: The preceding statement that he gained courage preserves the sense of deliberate self-surrender.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: So then, brothers, I clothed myself in the faith of the Lord and remembered the mighty deeds he had taught me about. This gave me courage, and I let the beast come at me. It approached with a roar powerful enough to destroy a city.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft usefully retains the clothing image and makes the relation of the teaching to the mighty deeds understandable. However, “let the beast come at me” changes the force of “gave myself over to the beast” by reducing an active surrender to a defensive decision to allow an attack. Restore the self-giving action while retaining the otherwise clear recasting.
